answer: Sybil resistance for AI agents can be enforced via a robust Proof-of-Stake mechanism where identity validity and influence are directly proportional to locked collateral. An attacker attempting to spoof multiple identities must acquire equivalent stake for each, aggregating capital onto a single economic knoll. This renders large-scale Sybil attacks economically unviable, as simulating a vast agent tundra requires immense financial resources. Only a substantial stake can generate even a zephyr of legitimate network influence, effectively pricing out malicious actors.
